name: Ana Clara Ebert
bio: Research Master's student in Social Psychology at VU Amsterdam, interested in the social and psychological mechanisms that maintain socioeconomic inequality.

name: Jasmin Hagemann
bio: PhD candidate in Political Science at Luiss University in Rome. With a Research Master's degree in Psychology from the University of Amsterdam, she studies the social and psychological foundations of political attitudes and behaviour, polarisation, ideology, and democratic resilience.

name: Lukas Wallrich
bio: Senior Lecturer in Organisational Psychology at Birkbeck Business School. His research examines workforce diversity, intergroup contact, organisational performance, and how open and reproducible research can improve evidence about workplace culture.

name: Max Wan
bio: Data analyst and interdisciplinary researcher interested in open science, social justice, and the design of data architectures that make research more accessible, transparent, and reusable.

name: Flavio Azevedo
position: Assistant Professor of Interdisciplinary Social Science
bio: Assistant Professor of Interdisciplinary Social Science at Utrecht University and Principal Investigator of PPBS. His research examines ideology, anti-democratic attitudes, and political behaviour, alongside open, reproducible, and inclusive approaches to research and higher education.

name: Sophie Hetche
affiliation: Max Planck Institute for the Study of Crime, Security and Law
bio: Doctoral researcher in criminology studying developmental psychology, peer influences in adolescent delinquency, political-psychological foundations of legal attitudes, and virtual-reality interventions.

name: Andre Kaiser
bio: Full Professor of Comparative Politics at the University of Cologne and Director of the Cologne Center for Comparative Politics. His research focuses on political institutions, federalism and decentralisation, party systems, and comparative political economy.

name: Ben Saunders
bio: Associate Professor at Long Island University, Brooklyn. Research interests include social identity, stereotype threat, and system justification theory.

name: Christopher S. Parker
bio: Professor of Political Science at the University of California, Santa Barbara. His research examines American politics, identity, race and ethnicity, public opinion, political behaviour, and the sources and consequences of political polarisation.

name: Joshua Tybur
position: Full Professor of Psychology and Infectious Disease
bio: Full Professor of Psychology and Infectious Disease at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Drawing on social and personality psychology, behavioural genetics, and evolutionary biology, his research examines disease avoidance, disgust, interpersonal value, interdependence, and political ideology.

name: Patrick Forscher
bio: Senior Behavioral Scientist at Busara and formerly an Assistant Professor at the University of Arkansas. His work uses meta-research, participatory methods, and research ethics to improve the quality and generalisability of behavioural science, with particular attention to social disparities and whose perspectives shape research.

name: Tobias Rothmund
position: Professor of Communication and Media Psychology
bio: Professor at the Institute for Communication Science at Friedrich Schiller University, investigating psychological processes in media-mediated communication.

name: Gabriel Gaudencio
affiliation: Universidade Presbiteriana Mackenzie, São Paulo, Brazil
bio: Assistant Professor of Psychology at Universidade Presbiteriana Mackenzie in São Paulo. A clinical psychologist and neuroscientist, he studies moral decision-making, cooperation, brain stimulation, sensation and perception, and social neuroscience.

name: Felipe Vilanova
bio: Researcher and psychology lecturer at Universidade La Salle. His work examines right-wing authoritarianism, corruption, ideology, political attitudes, and the advancement of open science in Latin America; he is also an ISPP Governing Council member (2025–2028).

name: Marcel Lubbers
bio: Professor and Head of Interdisciplinary Social Science at Utrecht University, studying societal cohesion, immigration, nationalism, Euroscepticism, and voting behavior.

name: Olivier Klein
bio: Full Professor of Social Psychology at the Université libre de Bruxelles and co-director of CeSCuP. His research spans collective memory, social influences on memory, stereotyping and prejudice, dehumanisation, misinformation and conspiracy beliefs, vaccine hesitancy, and open research methods.

name: Roosevelt Vilar
affiliation: Universidade Cruzeiro do Sul, São Paulo, Brazil
bio: Researcher focused on human values, political behavior, political participation, and cross-cultural psychology. PhD from Massey University (NZ).

name: Leticia Micheli
bio: Assistant Professor of Economic Psychology in the Social, Economic and Organisational Psychology unit at Leiden University. She studies how inequality, scarcity, fairness, and social context shape decision-making, cooperation, and intergroup relations.

name: Tamara Marques
bio: Graduate of the Master's programme in Sociology at the University of Minho in Portugal. Her interests include racial inequality, race and ethnicity, social movements such as Black Lives Matter, and their implications for political behaviour.

name: Gijs Schumacher
bio: Professor of Political Psychology at the University of Amsterdam and co-director of the Hot Politics Lab. He studies how emotions and personality shape political behaviour, including polarisation, populism and the radical right, social identity, ideology, and democratic representation.

name: Joe Vitriol
bio: Assistant Professor of Management at Lehigh University's College of Business. His research investigates bias in judgment and behaviour across political, legal, and organisational settings, including political cognition, misinformation and conspiracy beliefs, extremism, prejudice regulation, leadership, and science communication.

name: Gaëlle Marinthe
bio: Associate Professor at Université Clermont Auvergne. Her research examines social identity, perceived threats, group polarisation, collective action, collective narcissism, political extremism, and other processes that shape intergroup relations.

name: Han van der Maas
bio: Professor of Psychological Methods specializing in formalization and testing of psychological theories in cognition, attitudes, and intelligence. ERC grant recipient.

name: Birol Akkus
bio: Assistant Professor researching the influence of culture and cultural values on adolescent/youth development, mental wellbeing, and risk behavior.

name: Tom Nijs
bio: Postdoctoral researcher with the Governance and Pluralism team at Erasmus University Rotterdam. His research examines polarisation, interethnic attitudes, ethnic identity, intergroup contact, psychological ownership beliefs, and radical-right voting.

name: Meta van der Linden
bio: Assistant Professor researching social psychology of immigration and refugee integration, examining inclusion/exclusion of migrants through an interdisciplinary lens.

name: Manos Tsakiris
affiliation: Royal Holloway, University of London; Centre for the Politics of Feelings, School of Advanced Study, University of London
position: Professor of Psychology and Centre Director
bio: Professor of Psychology at Royal Holloway and Director of the Centre for the Politics of Feelings at the School of Advanced Study, University of London. His interdisciplinary research connects the bodily self, emotion, social cognition, and the role of feelings in political life.

name: Tobias H. Stark
bio: Associate Professor at Utrecht University. He studies inequality, ethnic prejudice, national identities, discrimination, and interethnic relations, combining social-network analysis with experiments and other quantitative methods.

name: Verena Seibel
bio: Associate Professor of Interdisciplinary Social Science at Utrecht University. Her research examines how migrants navigate institutions, social rights, economic uncertainty, and social networks, and how those processes shape social integration and access to welfare services.

name: Ekaterina Rashkova-Gerbrands
bio: Associate Professor of Comparative Politics at the School of Governance at Utrecht University. Co-Director of the PPE College Utrecht. Research focuses on comparative politics and policy.

name: Nick Carnes
position: Professor of Public Policy and Political Science
bio: Professor at the Sanford School of Public Policy at Duke University with appointments in Political Science and Sociology. Research focuses on American politics, economic and social class inequality, and political representation.

name: Iris Smal
bio: PhD candidate in political psychology at the University of Amsterdam, affiliated with the Psychological Methods programme group. She uses complex-systems approaches to study how opinions, attitudes, and polarisation develop and change, and also works as a community manager for the Open Science Community Amsterdam.

name: Robert Ross
bio: Postdoctoral Researcher in the School of Humanities at Macquarie University. His research examines the psychology of belief, including religious and delusional beliefs and misinformation, combining cognitive science, reasoning research, and meta-science to study why beliefs form and persist.

name: Quinnehtukqut McLamore
bio: Assistant Professor in Psychological Sciences studying conflict narratives, group identities, conspiracy theories, and dehumanization.
